review_note: Read the test and helpers line by line. Oracle is independent of drmTMB: base-R dense Laplace (sb26_laplace, own Newton loop and log-det) on hand-built kernels (Henderson tabular A from a 3-family full-sib pedigree with diag(A) > 1.6, hand relmat kernel at scale 1.6, hand exponential spatial kernel; Ainv and Q are solve() of those). The pedigree provider is checked against the hand A, not against package code. Each fit's logLik matches the oracle at the fitted parameters within 1e-4, and the oracle values agree across providers within 1e-6. Emulated bugs (swapped selector coefficient sets, reversed per-level SD, cov2cor(K), K x 2, kernel read by position) are each asserted to move the oracle by more than 0.1, which is 1000x the tolerance, in every b29b_check call; the file passed these. Every linked row_key is fitted: logit animal+relmat for A+K, A+Q, Ainv+K and pedigree+K; animal+spatial for A, Ainv and pedigree; animal-only A, Ainv and pedigree. Each field is an intercept-only term on its own grouping factor with sd(.) ~ z, so there is no unlabelled (1 + x | id) concern. All 9 sha256 values in the manifest and the receipt, manifest and test hashes in the fragment match the current files. Console shows 160 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, exit 0, and no live-Julia claim. Does NOT establish: animal Ainv+Q or pedigree+Q for logit (only A+Q is fitted); anything for probit or cloglog; slope, labelled or correlated blocks; calibration, coverage, SE, recovery or Julia parity; any seed other than the fixed ones (one seed per block); behaviour away from the fitted parameters, since the check is likelihood assembly and selector alignment at the optimum.
